info.name: Control-M Automation API
info.description:
Every Control-M Automation API (AAPI) call this project makes, as stand-alone requests - the five calls implemented in `src/ctm_client.py` and used by the job report pipeline (`src/ctm_job_report.py`).

The ServiceNow side of this project is a separate API - see the collection shipped with `4-ai-job-type-examples/service-now-incident` and `docs/snow_api_calls.md`.

## Auth

Every request sends the AAPI token as the `x-api-key` header (collection-level API-key auth). There is no login/logout session call - a persistent AAPI token is used directly. Generate the token in the Control-M Automation API UI.

## Setup

1. Open the collection **Variables** tab (or an environment) and fill in `controlm_url` (base URL **including** the `/automation-api` path) and `controlm_api_key`.
2. Set `ctm_server` + `order_id` to a real finished job (they come from a Control-M alert's `data_center` / `order_id` fields). A collection pre-request script builds `job_id` = `<ctm_server>:<order_id>` and percent-encodes the `:` to `%3A`, matching `ctm_client._job_id()`.
3. For the alert calls, set `alert_id` (the alert's `alert_id` field).

## Folders

- **1. Job detail** - `get_job_status()` / `get_job_output()` / `get_job_log()`, the three reads `build_job_report()` runs per job alert. Each is independent and allowed to fail on its own.
- **2. Alert mark-as-read** - `update_alert()` + `set_alert_status()`, run by `mark_alert_read()` once the job log has been captured.

See `docs/ctm_client.md` and `docs/ctm_alert_order.md` for the field-by-field notes and real captured responses.

item.name: 1. Job detail
item.description: The three read-only AAPI calls build_job_report() makes for a job alert (src/ctm_job_report.py). Order matches docs/ctm_alert_order.md: status, then output, then log.

exec: console.log(b.name, "->", b.status, "| start", b.startTime, "end", b.endTime || "(still running)");

request.description:
`ctm_client.get_job_status()`. Single-job endpoint (`/run/job/<jobId>/status`), **not** the bulk `/run/jobs/status?jobid=` list - the bulk list only covers Control-M's active pipeline and returns nothing once a job has finished, which is the common case here (alerts fire after a job has already ended). Returns the full job-status object as-is.

Sample response (from docs/ctm_alert_order.md):
```json
{
  "jobId": "ctm-lin-srv:003i7",
  "name": "ZZM PreFlight Check",
  "folder": "ZZM_UC_MULTIPATH_CLOUD",
  "status": "Ended Not OK",
  "startTime": "20260814235859",
  "endTime": "20260814235859",
  "ctm": "ctm-lin-srv",
  "host": "ctm-lin-agt.werkstatt.local",
  "outputURI": "https://.../run/job/ctm-lin-srv:003i7/output",
  "logURI": "https://.../run/job/ctm-lin-srv:003i7/log"
}
```
A non-200 raises in `ctm_client`; `build_job_report()` catches it and sets `job_status` to `null`.

`ctm_client.get_job_output()` - job stdout/sysout for one run. `ctm_job_report.py` passes the alert's own `run_counter` as `runNo` with leading zeros stripped (`"00003"` -> `3`); a job that has been rerun has more than one run's output, and the wrong `runNo` returns the wrong run. `run_no=0` (the default here) gets the most recent run.

Response is plain text, e.g.:
```
20260814235859 Failed to submit job.
20260814235859 Found empty sysout file.
...
```

`ctm_client.get_job_log()` - Control-M's own run log (submit / start / state-change / rerun events), **not** job stdout (that is Get Job Output). The log covers every run of the job. Response is plain text.

Capturing this successfully is what gates `mark_alert_read()` in folder 2 - the alert is only marked read once there is actually a log to point at.

item.name: 2. Alert mark-as-read
item.description: ctm_job_report.py's mark_alert_read() runs both of these once the job log has been captured, so anyone looking at the alert in Control-M can see where the report landed. Both are best-effort - a failure on either is logged, not fatal.

exec: // NOTE: the AAPI has been seen to return 200 with a \"successfully modified\"
// message WITHOUT the change taking effect. A 200 here is not proof the
// alert was updated - re-read the alert to confirm. See docs/ctm_client.md.

request.description:
`ctm_client.update_alert()`. Sets the alert's own comment/text field (and optionally `urgency` - add `"urgency": "..."` to the body). `ctm_job_report.py` sets the comment to the saved report's filename, e.g. `Job log saved: 2256.json`.

`alertIds` is a list - the AAPI takes more than one, this project always passes exactly one.

Sample response:
```json
{ "message": "[2256] The alert was successfully modified" }
```

exec: // Same caveat as Update Alert: a 200 does not guarantee the status
// actually changed. ctm_job_report.py persists the raw response body
// to data/job_report_tracking.json for exactly this reason.

request.description:
`ctm_client.set_alert_status()`. `ctm_job_report.py` calls this with `status="Reviewed"` to mark the alert as read once its log has been captured.

Control-M/EM re-emits this same alert back through the alert action as a `call_type='U'` update when the status changes - `ctm_alerts.sh`'s early-exit filter is what stops that echo from re-triggering either pipeline (see docs/ctm_alerts_sh.md).

Sample response:
```json
{ "message": "[2256] The alert status was successfully modified" }
```
